title: A clip splits into pieces, and the pieces can be moved
goal: Cutting is most of editing a recording: split a take where the fumble is, throw the bad piece away, slide what is left along, hold on a frame, and speed a dull stretch up. Work out and build the rules for all of that on their own, ahead of the timeline that shows them, so that the moment the open-a-recording question is answered the cutting underneath already works and is proved.
notes: Split out of cut-arrange-and-retime-what-is-on-the-timeline by the daily triage of 2026-09-20, the same way the model half of a-document-can-have-time came out as time-lives-in-the-document-and-a-layer-can-have earlier the same day. WHY: every p1 in the queue is blocked or waiting on a dependency, and the whole video chain hangs on one pending decision card about where a recording opens. The cutting RULES do not depend on that answer, so they can be built now. WHERE IT STANDS: Sources/PhotonzCore/VideoCuts.swift already has VideoCutList with split(atTimeline:), removePiece(at:) and keep(fromTimeline:), pieces held in play order, and no way to move one. Sources/PhotonzCore/DocumentTime.swift landed on 2026-09-20 with LayerTime (in, out, source offset, source length) and withIn/withOut/moved(toInMS:). This task is where those two meet: one piece model the new timeline will drive. WHAT IT MUST NOT DO: build the timeline gesture, move where a recording opens, or touch the old video editor. Those stay in cut-arrange-and-retime-what-is-on-the-timeline behind the card. UX-PATTERNS D18 and docs/design/video-surface.md settle the shape: a split adds a PIECE to a row, never a second row.
acceptance: A clip can be split at a moment into two pieces of the same clip, each with its own start and end, both still reading the same recording, and either piece can be split again
Pieces can be put in a different order, and what plays and what an export would write follow the new order with nothing else to change
Taking a piece out says what happens to the gap it leaves, and the same rule holds wherever a piece is removed or made longer
Trimming never destroys anything: a piece pulled in and back out returns to exactly what it started as, proved by a test
A held frame is a piece whose start and end are the same moment, and it behaves like any other piece
A piece can be given a speed, and what that does to its length and to its sound is written down and tested
Each of these is one step of undo
All of it is pure, value-typed and tested first, with no app or drawing types involved, and the tests come before the code
Nothing changes on screen and every walk that exists today still passes, untouched
The notes say exactly what is left for the timeline gesture task to do
